entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, a self-hosted server, and a cloud platform.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides long-term agent memory through retain, recall, and reflect operations. It can be deployed with Docker, pip, or Kubernetes and supports hosted and local LLM providers.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes resources, memories, and skills as files, with scoped semantic search across directories. It can archive sessions into inspectable Markdown memories and uses viking:// URIs with tiered L0/L1/L2 loading.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that gives agents persistent long-term memory across sessions through a self-hosted knowledge graph engine. It structures text as entities, relationships, and searchable chunks, and supports custom data models, ontologies, plugins, and MCP.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API that extracts conversation facts, reconciles contradictions, and handles automatic forgetting. Its connectors include Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and it processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports corrections and withdrawal. It shares memory across agents while keeping transient task state local, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents, tracking peers, sessions, and messages over time. It provides Python and TypeScript SDKs and supports managed, local, and self-hosted use.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git-like repository, with version control for a context tree and five-tier retrieval, four tiers of which are non-LLM. It also offers a React/Ink TUI and REPL, plus support for 20 LLM providers and 24 built-in agent tools.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes Agents with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; BEAM results are reported for v3.0.0, while LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts and consolidates memories across agents, reconciles conflicting information, and manages forgetting. It also supports memory exchange through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that combines vector search with structured facts, fabric recall, and an auto-curated wiki. It describes local infrastructure using Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and a Ground Truth hierarchy for prioritizing injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: AutoContext is a recursive self-improving context harness intended to help agents succeed on complex tasks. Runs can start from a plain-language goal or saved scenario, and their filesystem-based artifacts can be inspected, diffed, replayed, or exported.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches session histories already stored on disk across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenClaw, and other supported agents. It can also resume a session or continue it in another agent, and runs locally without a model or server.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: Hermes LCM is a Hermes Agent plugin that persists messages in SQLite using a hierarchical DAG. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from that history.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: Honcho Self-Hosted gives Hermes Agent private memory that persists across sessions. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: SignetAI provides a local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer for agents including Hermes Agent, Claude Code, and Codex. It connects through hooks, plugins, or extensions and can run on a local machine or as a team server, with a dashboard for browsing memory and asking questions.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memories as plain YAML files in an open engram format. It offers local search with keyword search as a fallback, plus a CLI and MCP server.
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can create session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, integrating through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory stores long-term agent memory locally in a SQLite file, with FTS5 search and a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore, without requiring a vector database or embeddings.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering for prefix-cache sharing, including for text and multimodal context. Its context index supports reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, and it integrates with Hermes Agent as well as vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: YantrikDB is a self-maintaining memory plugin for Hermes with an embedded backend by default and an HTTP option. Its recall results include a why_retrieved explanation, and it also supports memory canonicalization and contradiction tracking.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn uses an Obsidian vault as the source of truth for durable, cross-project memory, stored as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to coding agents.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: llm-wiki-cli is an agent-driven memory CLI that maintains source-grounded knowledge across sessions as a Wiki with citations and history. It does not require embeddings or a vector database.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: flowstate-qmd is an anticipatory memory system that watches agent session logs to prefetch context. It uses local SQLite-vec storage and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack brings Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace together under one memory owner for Hermes. It manages state and retrieval with SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma, then gives the agent a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep combines BM25 full-text search with ranked graph traversal to retrieve connected information. It automatically indexes codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, while edge tags make stored notes navigable in both directions.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema token use through local keyword-based ranking. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 or later, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible coding agents. Its workflows cover migration, handoffs, and memory proposals, with integrations that remain opt-in rather than enabling automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes plugin stores memory in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file. Its importance-weighted recall brings higher-priority memories forward during context prefetch, alongside BM25 keyword search and named graph relationships between entries.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, and hooks into pre-LLM calls and session-end events.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes Agentmemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer. It supports immediate event deletion and records prefetch operations in a trace.jsonl audit log.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind extracts the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, helping restore it before work continues. It offers goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes, skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and uses no summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: This Hermes plugin provides durable cross-session memory by communicating with XMemo over HTTPS. It supplies ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It offers tools for searching and manually storing memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: Sourcevault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with slash commands for search, file reads, context, and Q&A. It supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop, and includes repository sync and indexed git-history search commands.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers retrieval through HNSW ANN, sparse search, and FM-index search, and can run via native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory-management and knowledge-graph tools for Hermes Agent, with 17 tools for managing memories and traversing the graph. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can checkpoint context automatically during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit focuses on memory curation: it reviews plain Markdown files for stale or conflicting facts and proposes evidence-cited JSON diffs for review. A local Git repository tracks changes and lets you revert them, without using a database.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers provides an agentic skills framework and software development workflow covering specification, planning, and subagent-driven development. Its skills trigger automatically in supported coding-agent harnesses, and its README includes installation instructions for multiple coding agents.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins, and its CLI supports Hermes Agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This collection provides structured skills across 34 security domains, with mappings to MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. It is listed as compatible with more than 26 AI platforms.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: This skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable draw.io files. It supports incremental sync that preserves manual layout and annotations, and includes the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court provides a master router and connector skills for agent-to-agent commerce, alongside vendored copies of official protocol skills. It also adds verification and dispute resolution.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: This project detects writing patterns and offers a rewrite mode with up to two editing passes. Its in-place editing refuses source code, configuration, and generated data, while the detector can score files or piped text.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw unifies skills across agents and devices, with integrations for Hermes, Codex, Claude Code, and other agents. Its dashboard covers skills, validation, versions, and session traces.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills, and supports Claude Code, Codex, and agent-plugins.org specifications. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This collection offers professional agent skills with frameworks, output templates, quality checks, and anti-patterns; the README describes 21 skills designed for unattended use. Install it with `npx pm-claude-skills add` or through Claude Code's plugin directory.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: These skills support YouTube transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction for Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor. They require a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: This Hermes meta-skill plugin detects and proposes reusable skills from active workflows, then generates SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super Hermes generates custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. It reports findings alongside a report of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, including remote skill registries sourced from Git and S3. It also provides tools for reading bundled resources and running scripts in a sandbox that isolates untrusted code from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that weave prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files from them with a tangler. When source files change, it syncs those edits back into the literate document, making it useful for keeping code and documentation together.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexities, while a spec review gate evaluates documents with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents with structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute approach. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, along with CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also provides a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models, pairing work memory with a path to model handoff.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format, alongside guides on topics including installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. It belongs in this list as a community resource for Portuguese-speaking users, with contributions submitted through pull requests.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting skills for FLUX image and video generation, plus BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills, giving users a focused set of resources for image and video workflows.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills spec, for oracle network and smart contract interactions. The README describes the repository as community examples only and gives an npx command for installing it.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with both automated and step-by-step workflows. Skill testing and export make it a practical entry for building and preparing agentskills.io-compliant skills.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika describes itself as a workflow language for AI, with workflows checked before a model is called and runs available with a model the user chooses. It records runs in a verifiable hash chain, making run history a defining part of the project.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python SkilldockClient and a CLI. It supports installation with recursive dependency resolution and includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in checkpoints and rollback procedures provide a route to recovery when execution needs to be revisited.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills, with federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification and operates autonomously via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye retrieves relevant skills through five layers, including hard triggers and semantic embeddings. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token usage; it can also degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard runs read-only adversarial code reviews, using parallel subagents to examine edge cases, adversarial concerns, and integration. A deterministic pre-scan and proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox help verify and triage findings without changing code.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is a personal execution system where recurring habits are scored daily and tasks cover other activities. It runs locally with SQLite, includes an Android client, and connects to agents over MCP.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill coordinates Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness sub-agents to simplify code. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, with tiered application and an approval gate.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: Hermes Cybersec Lab brings together cybersecurity skills and tools, with highlights including 2,077 skills across repositories and 131+ tools for network work, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes structures tasks into multiple stories with mandatory evidence-based verification gates. It also provides a systematic protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io for C# and .NET, using SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.doomsday-network/bounty-guard: Bounty Guard scans untrusted GitHub issues and repositories for prompt injection, CI secret exfiltration, and cryptographic bounty escrow. It is a dependency-free Python 3.9+ CLI with GitHub Action support and hosted HTTP or local stdio MCP options, alongside a published honeypot list and machine-readable threat feed.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time observability dashboard for tracking token costs, session history, and skill analytics. It keeps data access read-only and local, with log desensitization and optional incident alerts via Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: A collection of plain Markdown skills for code review and session management, including multi-session reconciliation and worktree recovery. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer, making this a practical set of workflows for Hermes Agent users.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This Claude Code skill creates reproducible demo GIFs for repository READMEs, generating recording scripts with vhs or Playwright and optimizing files toward a target size under 8 MB. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, so it covers more than browser-only demos.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: This project builds Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly for field drift, making it useful for creating skills that stay aligned with their specifications.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: A CLI and MCP server for searching more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, with direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its support for MCP-compatible clients including Hermes makes it a discovery and installation option for Hermes Agent users.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: This host-agnostic feedback loop fetches sessions, indexes installed skills, and drafts structured improvement proposals. Proposals are review-only by default, with optional auto-apply gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, or regression evaluators.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage packages skills and blueprints for social data, web research, and enrichment; its packaged skills combine an agent, skills, and a data flow. Community skills are also welcome in the project's `skills/community/` directory.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: A set of Hermes Agent skills for routing file operations with environment-specific path syntax and selecting and verifying existing, project-compatible Python interpreters. It supports native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL environments.
entries.doomsday-network/web3-agent-skills: This pack connects to the Remote MCP server at doomsday.network/mcp and includes scripts for bounty scanning and pool mining. It brings those Web3-related skills to agents that can use the provided skill files or MCP connection.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This collection includes tools to transcribe Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, remove common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extract structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. It brings video, text, and document-processing tasks together in a set of Hermes skills.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets agents find open support bounties, buy ticket context, and submit answers for review; a human approves the winning answer. It also supports creating a bounty board and provides public wallet earnings records.
entries.f-o-x11/deed-page-skill: This agent skill publishes static files to a permanent deed.page URL with one curl request and no account. It also includes a hosted remote MCP server and can be installed with `npx skills add`.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: This skill automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Skillseal tests AI agent skills for structure, functionality, and security in isolated Docker containers. It belongs in this list as a way to check that a skill works and provide an Ed25519-signed certificate that can be verified through its public API.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server, with 191 tools and five ready-to-use workflow skills. It also supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands, making it an option for teams using those agent environments.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: Alphapipeline provides risk checks for tokens, including honeypot, tax, and liquidity risks, alongside market data such as DEX slippage and funding rates. Its REST endpoints and remote MCP server make those checks and data available to AI agents.
entries.NickSF189/kisscode-agent: Kisscode-agent is a skill for AI agents to join KissCode, supplied as SKILL.md and HEARTBEAT.md. It includes installation instructions for several agent environments and mirrors kisscode.ai/skill.md.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: China Briefing generates structured Chinese news reports at multiple geographic scales, from global to street level, with core conclusions and action suggestions. It also uses semantic memory of user interests to expand searches, distinguishing it as a briefing skill with personalized search.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: Astro Agents MCP provides deterministic Western and Vedic astrology results, with SHA-256 hashes for verification. Its MCP endpoint requires no authentication, and it offers per-call REST payment through x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: A progressive MCP client that incrementally discovers server metadata and tool schemas, using three-layer loading to minimize token usage. Its socket-based daemon architecture maintains persistent connections, making it a distinctive skill for agents that need on-demand access to MCP tools.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This Nix project packages AI coding agents and development tools, including Hermes, and automatically updates its packages daily. Its README provides `nix run` commands for the listed tools, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw setup and access to device hardware and UI through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This project provides a Termux installer and guide for running Hermes Agent on Android, using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models through Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct and CRD-based deployment workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, and scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, and alert rules, with access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image with mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports declarative Hermes deployment, including configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first web control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances, each with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes-OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This project provides a Helm chart for running Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation options via an OCI registry or a published Helm repository. Provider-specific values examples and CI installation on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a deployment option with documented configuration examples and a Kubernetes install check.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a local project graph with `codegraph init` and automatically syncs it as files change. Its MCP server connects the pre-indexed graph to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, aiming to reduce token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token usage and costs across Hermes and other AI coding agents, then presents usage summaries, statistics, and session details in a dashboard. It also lets users submit data to a leaderboard and create a public profile.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor displays real-time token use, costs, and rate limits across 46+ AI coding tools and providers, including Hermes Agent. It also provides historical trends and breakdowns, with multi-device sync.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for inspecting coding-agent API traffic, including prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage. It can compare adjacent requests to show context changes and redact common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design skills, UI prompts, and layout guidance for building interfaces with AI. It supports providers that accept Markdown or general prompting and connects to coding tools through TypeUI MCP or plugins.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an installable workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It includes product-development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop with seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for skins and themes for the Hermes terminal UI. Users can create skins with YAML files, and custom skins inherit unspecified values from the default skin.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks agent-facing content in project directories, including configs, tool descriptions, and system prompts, using HERM v1.1 scoring. Its findings include file locations and suggested fixes, and it supports CI gates and reviewed baselines.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce using Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser for autonomous agent control via MCP, with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other providers. Its supervisor sidebar manages approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads, and it supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, running natively in Claude Code without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages with two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin automatically captures and recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for token-saving CLI workflows, with the project highlighting 90–99% token savings. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, plus automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md provides a framework for creating Hermes Agents scoped to individual folders, with local configuration and skills. It supports switching between default and scoped agents, and lets projects use their own memories, tools, and instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of hermes-agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This migration tool transfers OpenClaw files—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats, and can set up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: observeco is a native Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations and monitors multi-agent systems in two modes: passive analysis without token use and scheduled active probing. Its config-aware baselines are designed to detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.doomsday-network/cuda-gpu-miner: This project provides a standalone pool miner that runs with Python, alongside README instructions for CUDA GPU mining through the Doomsday repository. It also documents cloud GPU deployment with RunPod and Vast.ai.
entries.doomsday-network/github-bounty-scanner: This scanner searches GitHub issues for bounty, USDC, wDOOM, and Algora opportunities, then classifies results into three bounty-safety categories. Its quickstart uses Python’s standard library.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds voice interaction to Hermes Agent, with wake-word support and adaptive turn-taking that includes barge-in. It runs offline without API keys or accounts and supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup is a local runtime for working toward online income opportunities, operating by default with deterministic behavior and no network access. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.doomsday-network/doom-pay: DoomPay provides a self-custodial crypto checkout for DOOM and wDOOM, with HTML buttons and programmatic checkout calls. Checkout sessions can also be created through an API, while a Python SDK and MCP server support payment verification.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: hermes-memoss is a memory plugin with semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It provides tools to search, add, and delete memories, and includes a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: cc-switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other coding-agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts in one place, with versions for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with 21 built-in professional assistants. It also supports remote access through a WebUI and messaging platforms, and runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides web and phone access to Hermes Agent, with a three-panel layout for sessions, chat, and workspace files. Its file browser includes inline previews, and the project is designed for access through an SSH tunnel.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: This desktop companion helps users install, configure, and chat with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI also manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools; the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a web dashboard for managing Hermes Agent chats, sessions, and integrations with Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp. It also offers visual workflows with schedules and approval gates, and is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, and Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace brings chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector into a native web workspace. Its features include role-based Swarm Mode with tmux-backed workers, an MCP catalog, and a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative coding workspace that gathers sessions from Hermes and other agents in a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate work across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH, with views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs. Its embedded terminal provides direct shell access for system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent, with support for Windows and macOS and native window and process management. It includes a Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, plus interfaces for chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime, including Hermes Cloud and self-hosted connections. It offers a Bot Mode for agent switching and group chats; Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for controlling a self-hosted Hermes agent by pairing with a hermes-webui server. It supports streamed chats with file or image attachments, server-session search and resumption, and views for scheduled tasks, skills, memory, and insights.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, while a live workspace shows code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: This interactive TUI has nine tabs and four selectable color themes for monitoring Hermes. It tracks agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and includes a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS session browser and agent cockpit helps users search prompts, tool activity, errors, and file paths across Hermes and other coding-agent CLIs. It also tracks Codex and Claude quota burn per session, with a search index built locally.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted web dashboard brings a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel together for the Hermes AI agent stack. It also provides real-time chat with tool-call visualization, MCP server lifecycle controls, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: This native macOS workspace runs Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud computers and SSH hosts, with one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers. It also includes WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable mission-control dashboard template pairs with a local Hermes agent through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox surfaces requests with side effects for review.
entries.liftaris/herm: This alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard connects to the Hermes Agent gateway. Its tabs cover profiles, sessions, skills, cron, and memory, while kanban boards, task details, diagnostics, and dispatch controls support agent operations.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run React SPA provides a 10-page, mobile-first dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. It combines terminal chat with streaming responses and file attachments, Telegram validation using dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication, and background spawning for up to five concurrent agent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: This portable Hermes Agent desktop for Windows offers a dark-themed GUI with multilingual support and session management. Its highlights include workflow automation, runtime tool creation, and local-model support through LM Studio.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: This self-hosted web interface pairs a glassmorphic chat experience with real-time log streaming. It also includes a file browser, task tracking dashboard, and management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: This dashboard focuses on monitoring and configuring Hermes, with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It supports inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, while keeping configuration and environment-variable views read-only.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: This self-hosted AI workspace centers on chat with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. It also offers a marketplace for discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, plus isolated profiles for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client supports collaboration among 20 specialized AI agents, with a PM orchestrator and streaming chat. Its visual Skill Store offers 50+ curated one-click installations, and the client also supports model switching.
entries.nicolasestrem/hermes-model-switcher: This plugin lets you switch models across Hermes Agent profiles from the Web Dashboard, with configured routes shown together in one matrix. It previews changes before applying them and includes named presets and guarded Undo.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: This unofficial, open-source interactive chat client for self-hosted Hermes Agent supports Android, web, macOS, and Linux alpha. It adds command approvals, live tool-step updates, and interactive answer cards for checklists, choices, forms, rankings, and votes.
